Summarise an edge mixture model

Source: R/bison_mixture.R
summary.bison_mixture.Rd

Summarises the results of bison_mixture(). Printing the summary shows the most probable number of components and its probability, the probability of each number of components, and, for the most probable number, the posterior median of each component mean (on the natural scale) and the probability of the first few edges belonging to each component.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bison_mixture'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A bison_mixture object from bison_mixture().

...

Not used.

Value

A summary.bison_mixture object, which is printed as described above.

See also

get_network_component_probabilities(), get_edge_component_probabilities(), get_component_means() for the same results as data frames.

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model_mixture(
  "count", num_components = 2, component_weights = c(0.5, 0.5)
)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "count_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("count_conjugate")
)
fit_mixture <- bison_mixture(fit_edge, num_components = 3, verbose = FALSE)
summary(fit_mixture)
#> === Fitted dyadic mixture model ===
#> Maximum number of components: 3
#> Most probable number of components: 2
#> Posterior probability: 100%
#> === Component probabilities ===
#>        1 2 3
#> P(K=k) 0 1 0
#> === Component means (K = 2) ===
#>            1      2
#> median 0.093 11.778
#> === Edge component probabilities (K = 2) ===
#>         1 2
#> 1 <-> 2 1 0
#> 1 <-> 3 0 1
#> 1 <-> 4 1 0
#> 1 <-> 5 1 0
#> 1 <-> 6 0 1
#> 1 <-> 7 0 1
#> ... (99 more rows; see get_edge_component_probabilities())
